matt-marble-stone-pebbles-9: In Japanese gardens, raked pebbles represent flowing water — the tradition is over a thousand years old.
matt-marble-stone-pebbles-8: Decorative stone keeps weeds down and moisture in — one of the few garden jobs done once that lasts years.
matt-marble-stone-pebbles-7: No two marble pebbles are identical — veining patterns are as individual as fingerprints.
matt-marble-stone-pebbles-6: Pebbles at the base of a pot improve drainage — water flows freely through the gap instead of pooling at the rim.
matt-marble-stone-pebbles-copy: Tumbled marble gets its smooth edges from rotating drums — the same way river stones are worn round, just faster.
matt-marble-stone-pebbles-5: A pebble mulch reflects warmth back into the soil in winter and shields it from sun in summer.
matt-marble-stone-pebbles-3: Stone top-dressing anchors lightweight pots — a useful trick for balconies that get gusty in monsoon.
matt-marble-stone-pebbles-2: Stone mulch never feeds termites or fungi the way wood chips can — which is why it's preferred indoors.
matt-marble-stone-pebbles: Marble pebbles are graded by size — uniform sizing is what makes the finished surface look intentional rather than poured.
arty-rect-set-of-6-with-plants: Ready-planted sets remove the hardest part of plant styling — choosing pots that suit both the plants and each other.
arty-rect-set-of-8: Odd numbers of planters look natural to the eye — even rows feel formal, asymmetry feels designed.
arty-rect-set-of-5: Grouping planters in threes and fives at varied heights is a classic styling rule called 'the triangle'.
arty-rectangle: Rectangular planters line up neatly along walls and railings — the shape makes the most of narrow spaces.
bello-hook-pot: Hook pots use the most overlooked garden space — the air above your head.
bello-square-20-colour-set-of-9: A nine-colour set turns a plain wall into a feature — matching pots read as furniture, mismatched ones read as a garden.
